linkedin.post:
Ontario wine keeps proving there is still room for experimentation, even in a region that already has clear strengths.

Leaning Post Wines recently made what appears to be Ontario’s first single-variety Dolcetto, using fruit from just twelve rows at its Senchuk Vineyard in Niagara’s Lincoln Lakeshore sub-appellation.

That kind of small-scale planting says a lot about the mindset behind the project: curiosity, patience, and a willingness to test what can thrive here.

Dolcetto is a grape most closely associated with Piedmont, and it is still unusual to see it bottled on its own in Ontario. For trade and wine lovers alike, this is a reminder that Niagara is still evolving in ways worth paying attention to.

At $45, the 2023 release also fits into a broader conversation about how niche, site-driven wines are finding their place with curious consumers.
